notes.GLP1-047-UC-001:
URGENT CARE — 09/09/2025

CC: sinus congestion and facial pain.
HPI: 41 y/o F with 10 days of nasal congestion, thick yellow-green drainage, pressure over both cheeks and forehead, upper tooth ache on the right, worse when bending forward. Improved around day 5, then worsened again over the last 3 days with low-grade fever (100.4 at home). Mild cough from postnasal drip. No vision changes, no periorbital swelling, no severe headache, no neck stiffness. Tried saline spray and OTC decongestant with minimal relief.
ROS: fatigue; otherwise negative — no chest pain, no dyspnea, no rash.
Meds: sertraline, sumatriptan PRN, vitamin D, ibuprofen PRN, triamcinolone cream PRN. Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: T 100.1, HR 88, BP 122/76, SpO2 98%. Bilateral maxillary tenderness, purulent drainage in posterior pharynx, nasal mucosa edematous. TMs clear. No periorbital edema, EOMI. Neck supple. Lungs clear.
Assessment: acute bacterial rhinosinusitis ("double worsening").
Plan: amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg BID x 7 days; saline irrigation BID; fluticasone nasal spray; acetaminophen/ibuprofen PRN. Avoid decongestants on days she uses sumatriptan. Return precautions reviewed: high fever, facial swelling, vision changes, severe headache.
notes.GLP1-047-OSR-001:

Source: Lakeside Periodontics

Request for medical clearance for osseous surgery (upper right quadrant) under local anesthesia with possible oral sedation (triazolam).
Medical history per dental office form: migraine, anxiety, eczema, low back pain. Medications listed: sertraline 50 mg, sumatriptan PRN, vitamin D, ibuprofen PRN, triamcinolone cream. No anticoagulants or antiplatelets. No bisphosphonates. No history of endocarditis, prosthetic valves, or joint replacements.
Response (covering provider): no contraindication to local anesthesia with epinephrine. Triazolam acceptable; note additive sedation with sertraline is minimal, but she should have a driver. No antibiotic prophylaxis indicated. Cleared for procedure without restrictions.

notes.GLP1-047-UC-002:
URGENT CARE — 12/04/2025

CC: cough, congestion, sinus pressure.
HPI: 41 y/o F with 10 days of congestion and facial pressure, now with thick discolored drainage and worsening right-sided maxillary pain for 3 days after initial improvement. Subjective fevers. Similar episode in September treated with amoxicillin-clavulanate with full resolution. No vision changes, no periorbital swelling, no severe headache. Cough mostly at night from drainage.
ROS: fatigue, mild sore throat. Negative for chest pain, shortness of breath, abdominal pain, rash.
PMH: migraine, anxiety, eczema, low back pain, recurrent sinusitis x2 this year.
Meds: sertraline 50 mg daily, sumatriptan PRN, vitamin D3, ibuprofen PRN, triamcinolone cream PRN. NKDA.

Exam: Wt 103.1 kg. T 99.9, HR 84, BP 118/74, SpO2 99%. Right maxillary tenderness; purulent drainage; nasal turbinates edematous. TMs normal. Oropharynx mildly erythematous. Neck: shotty anterior cervical nodes. Lungs clear, no wheeze.

Plan: doxycycline 100 mg BID x 7 days (recent amoxicillin-clavulanate); saline irrigation; fluticasone nasal spray daily. If a third episode occurs within 12 months, consider ENT referral and CT sinuses. Return precautions discussed.

notes.GLP1-047-ORTH-002:
ORTHOPEDICS CONSULT — 02/04/2026

CC: bilateral anterior knee pain.
HPI: 41 y/o F with 6 weeks of aching anterior knee pain, right worse than left, worse with stairs, squatting, and prolonged sitting ("theater sign"). No trauma, locking, or giving way. No swelling. She remains in the weight program started in the winter and has been riding the stationary bike and walking daily — pain started after she increased bike resistance quickly.
PMH: left shoulder impingement (improved after 2025 injection), low back pain, migraine, anxiety.
Exam: normal gait. No effusion. Patellar tracking with mild lateral tilt; positive patellar grind bilaterally; J-sign absent. Full ROM. Ligaments stable (Lachman, varus/valgus, posterior drawer negative). McMurray negative. Hip abductor weakness 4/5 bilaterally. Tight IT bands and hamstrings.
Imaging: knee X-rays (3 views bilateral) — normal joint spaces, no patella alta, no osteophytes.
Assessment: bilateral patellofemoral pain syndrome.
Plan: PT referral for hip/quad strengthening; lower bike resistance and raise seat height; ice after activity; ibuprofen PRN with food; avoid deep squats for 4–6 weeks. Follow-up in 8 weeks or sooner if swelling or mechanical symptoms.

notes.GLP1-047-DERM-002:
DERMATOLOGY — 05/20/2026

CC: itchy rash under the breasts.
HPI: 42 y/o F with 3 weeks of itching and burning under both breasts and in the lower abdominal fold, worse with heat and humidity. Tried OTC hydrocortisone with minimal help.
Exam: symmetric, well-demarcated erythematous macerated plaques in inframammary folds and lower abdominal fold with satellite papules/pustules. KOH positive for budding yeast.
Assessment: intertrigo with cutaneous candidiasis.
Plan: nystatin powder BID x 2–3 weeks; keep folds dry (moisture-wicking fabric in folds, cool air drying after showers); avoid occlusive creams; stop OTC hydrocortisone. Rosacea stable on metronidazole gel. Follow-up PRN.
notes.GLP1-047-DERM-003:
DERMATOLOGY — 06/04/2026

CC: spotty discoloration on upper back and chest.
HPI: 42 y/o F with 4–6 weeks of light-colored, slightly scaly spots on the upper back, shoulders, and chest, more noticeable after sun exposure; mildly itchy. She has been sweating more since exercising regularly with the weight program.
PMH: rosacea, intertrigo (May 2026, resolved), eczema, migraine, anxiety.
Exam: multiple hypopigmented, finely scaling, coalescing macules on upper back, shoulders, and upper chest. Evoked scale positive. Wood's lamp: faint yellow-green fluorescence. KOH: "spaghetti and meatballs" hyphae and spores.
Assessment: tinea (pityriasis) versicolor.
Plan: ketoconazole 2% shampoo as body wash — apply to affected areas for 5 minutes, then rinse, daily x 2 weeks, then weekly for maintenance during summer; shower soon after workouts; loose breathable clothing. Pigment will take weeks to months to even out after the yeast is treated. Follow-up PRN.
notes.GLP1-047-PCP-001:
PRIMARY CARE PROGRESS NOTE
Date: 08/04/2026

S: 42 y/o F, multi-problem visit.
1) Reflux: heartburn 2–3 nights/week, worse after late dinners and coffee; no dysphagia, weight loss, or GI bleeding.
2) Sleep: difficulty falling asleep, phone use in bed, wakes unrefreshed; no witnessed apneas or loud snoring per partner.
3) Knee pain follow-up: patellofemoral pain much better after 6 PT sessions; doing home strengthening.
4) Weight: weight 101.8 kg today vs 103.1 kg in the winter despite staying with the program (-1.3%). Frustrated. Asks about medication. No MTC/MEN2 history, no pancreatitis, no gallbladder disease. Uses IUD.
Also: tinea versicolor improving; migraine ~1/month, sumatriptan effective; mood stable on sertraline.

O: Wt 101.8 kg, BMI 34.4. BP 116/76, HR 74.
Gen: well. HEENT normal. Neck: no thyromegaly. CV: RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen: soft, mild epigastric tenderness, no masses. Knees: no effusion, mild patellar grind. Skin: fading hypopigmented macules on upper back.

A/P:
1. Reflux — avoid meals within 3 hours of bedtime, limit coffee after noon, elevate head of bed; if not improved in 4–6 weeks, start acid suppression.
2. Insomnia — sleep hygiene reviewed (consistent wake time, no screens 1 hour before bed, bed for sleep only); CBT-I app recommended; follow-up if not improved.
3. Patellofemoral pain — improving; continue home exercises.
4. Obesity, BMI 34.4 — Plan: start semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly (Wegovy) with standard dose titration; counseled on GI side effects (may transiently worsen reflux). Recheck in 3 months.
5. Health maintenance — flu vaccine in the fall.
